purpose: rapidcsv is a header-only C++ CSV parser library.

functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRowIdx: Returns the zero-based data row index for a given row label. Use it only when row labels are enabled and unique; otherwise it returns -1. It subtracts the header offset, and indices > INT_MAX aren’t supported.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::RemoveColumn: Removes a column by zero-based index/name from all data rows. It maps to the data-column index, erases that element from each row, and throws `std::out_of_range` if the column doesn’t exist on a row. Then it updates column names.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumn: `GetColumn` reads one CSV column into `vector<T>`, by zero-based index or header name, using default or custom conversion. It skips label rows. If a row lacks the column, it throws `out_of_range`. Example: `doc.GetColumn<float>("Close")`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::RemoveRow: Removes a row from the CSV document by zero-based data-row index (or by row label via the other overload). If the resolved row exists, it erases it and updates row names; otherwise it throws `std::out_of_range`.
functions.rapidcsv::Converter::ToStr: `ToStr` converts a numeric `T` to its CSV string form. Use/override `Converter<T>::ToStr()` for custom formatting. It uses `ostringstream`; float/double get 9/17 digits. Docs show overriding conversion via specialization and mention `test035.cpp`.
functions.rapidcsv::Converter<std::basic_string<ch: `Converter<string>::ToStr` is the string-specialized output conversion used by rapidcsv to turn numeric/char values into text. Use/override it via `Converter<T>::ToStr()` specializations. Floats use precision 9, doubles 17; other integral types stream normally.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetColumnName: `SetColumnName` assigns/updates a header name for a zero-based column. It requires a valid column-name row index; otherwise it throws `out_of_range`. It updates the name map, removes any old name, and grows the table as needed to store the new label.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumnNames: Returns all column names from the label row, starting after the row-name column. Use it to inspect/check column existence, e.g. `find(columnNames,"A")`. If no column labels are configured or the offset is invalid, it returns an empty vector.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::InsertColumn: `InsertColumn` inserts a new column at `pColumnIdx` in the CSV data. Use `pColumn` to fill it; if empty, it creates a blank column sized to current data rows. `pColumnName` sets the header label. It converts values to strings and aligns them with label/header offsets.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumnName: Returns the header/name for a zero-based data column. Use it with a valid column index; it maps to the data column via `GetDataColumnIndex`. If `mColumnNameIdx < 0`, it throws `std::out_of_range`; otherwise it returns the name from the header row.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetCell: GetCell retrieves one CSV cell by zero-based indices or by column/row labels, converting the stored string to T via standard conversion or a custom ConvFunc. Examples show string/numeric reads. It uses at(). Out-of-range/missing labels will fail.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::Load: `Load` populates a `Document` from a CSV file path or binary input stream, storing parse params then calling `ReadCsv()`. Use it with label/separator/converter/line-reader settings; docs show file, stream/stringstream, and comment-line skipping examples.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumnIdx: Returns the zero-based data-column index for a header name. Use it after column labels are loaded. If labels are disabled or the name isn’t found, it returns -1. Duplicate column names make the result undefined.
functions.rapidcsv::Converter<std::basic_string<ch: `ToVal` converts a CSV string to a numeric `T` for `Converter<T>`. It’s meant to be specialized/overridden for custom parsing. Uses `stoi/stol/stoll`; `int` is direct, small integer types are range-checked. Example: README `Converter<int>::ToVal`; note test035.cpp.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::InsertRow: Design: insert a data row at zero-based `pRowIdx`, optionally with values and a row label. Use `pRow` for cell data; if empty, it creates a blank row sized to current columns. If `pRowIdx` is past end, it pads with empty rows, then inserts.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRow: `GetRow` returns a row as `std::vector<T>`, by row label or zero-based index. Use the overload with `ConvFunc<T>` for custom conversion; otherwise it converts automatically. If the row name isn’t found, it throws `std::out_of_range`. Example: `doc.GetRow<std::string>("2017-02-22")`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetRowName: Sets the name for the zero-based row `pRowIdx`. It updates the row-name map, resizes `mData` if needed, and writes `pRowName` into the configured row-name column. If row-name column index < 0, it throws `std::out_of_range`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::Save: `Document::Save` writes the CSV data back out. Use `Save(path)` to save to a new file and update the document’s stored path; use `Save(stream)` to write to an output stream. If `path` is empty, it saves using the existing stored path.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRowNames: `GetRowNames()` returns all row labels from the row-name column, but only if `mRowNameIdx >= 0`; otherwise it returns an empty vector. Use it to inspect/check row names, e.g. for existence tests. Docs mention it alongside `GetColumnNames()`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetRow: `SetRow` writes a row into the CSV by row index or row name. It auto-expands `mData` if the target row doesn’t exist, and enlarges columns if `pRow` is wider than the current table. Values are converted to strings and stored after the row-name column offset.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetColumn: `SetColumn` writes a whole column into the CSV by index or name. It auto-expands rows/columns if needed, converts each value to string, and stores it at the data-column position. Use it to replace/add column data; out-of-range input causes the document to grow.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetCell: `SetCell` writes a value into the CSV at a given cell, using row/column indices or names. It auto-expands rows/columns if needed, converts `T` to string, then stores it. Use it to update/create cells; out-of-range data area is grown, not rejected.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumnCount: Returns the number of data columns, excluding label columns. Use it to inspect the current CSV layout. It counts columns from the first data row, subtracting row-name labels; if no data row exists or labels exceed columns, it returns 0.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRowName: `GetRowName(pRowIdx)` returns the row label at a zero-based data row index. It’s meant for CSVs configured with `LabelParams` and `pRowNameIdx` set (e.g. 0). If `mRowNameIdx < 0`, it throws `out_of_range`; it also uses `at()`, so bad indices can throw. No direct example shown.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRowCount: `GetRowCount()` returns the number of data rows, excluding any header/label rows. Use it to inspect how many rows of actual CSV data are available. It computes `mData.size() - (columnNameIdx + 1)` and clamps negatives to `0`.
functions.rapidcsv::Converter::ToVal: `ToVal()` converts a CSV string to numeric `T` for `Converter`. Use/override it to customize parsing; docs show specializing `Converter<int>::ToVal` and mention `ToVal()`/`ToStr()` can be overridden. It handles type-specific conversions and range checks for small integer types.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::Clear: `Clear()` resets a `rapidcsv::Document` to an empty state: it removes all loaded cell data, column names, and row names, and clears encoding flags (`Utf16`, endianness, UTF-8 BOM). Use it to reuse the same `Document` after discarding current contents.
functions.rapidcsv::no_converter::what: `rapidcsv::no_converter::what()` is the exception message accessor. It’s used when rapidcsv can’t convert a CSV field to the requested type. Calling `what()` returns the fixed string `"unsupported conversion datatype"`; it has no other behavior.
